findings.summary: Dependents list omits steward::queued_work, which re-checks stored readings with check_reading_text and drops proposed requests that now fail
findings.evidence: steward.rs:420-425: `if let Some(latest) = j.latest_reading() { if crate::reading::check_reading_text(latest, &request.text) != ReadingCheck::Accept { return None; } read = true; }`. The doc at steward.rs:399 says such a request is 'left out until a person runs `athena go`'. The drain module doc (drain.rs:100-106) says the same. The plan lists check_reading_text's callers as only `athena check-reading` and the replay. Once check_defined_terms lands, any proposed request already read under the old rules whose plain prose uses tier, layer, ladder or rung, including an approval whose title uses a term, drops out of `athena plan` and the drain. Nothing tells anyone. No test or doc in the plan covers this. Fix: Add steward::queued_work (the drain and `athena plan` queue listing) to Dependents. Add a test, for example in refusal_corpus.rs or using queued_work's public path if one exists: a proposed request whose prose uses 'tier' and whose stored reading has no Term line is left out (or re-read), and one with a Term line is listed read. State in D164 and the CHANGELOG that queued requests read before this change and using a term are held until re-read or `athena go`. If that is not intended, propose re-reading them unread instead and name it out of scope.

findings.summary: Criterion 7's 'give the loop-replay measured share if it differs' is only reported in the output, never written into the docs
findings.evidence: Criterion 7: 'The doc comment on check_defined_terms and D164 ... give the loop-replay measured share if it differs.' Step 8: 'Leave the 3% estimate and the replay-record statement as written. If a held send-back arrives ... report the measured share from the send-back in the output.' The send-back text (producer.rs:61-68) does carry the measured percentage, so the producer has the figure in the one case it can know. Fix: In step 8, when a held send-back arrives, also add the measured share from replay_problem to the check_defined_terms doc comment, the CHANGELOG entry and D164, next to the 3% estimate (labelled 'measured by the loop replay'). Leave the declared figure in the reading unchanged.

findings.summary: The generated-text skips match other modules' text shapes; one structural marker would be sounder
findings.evidence: plain_request_prose hard-codes anchor sentences and line prefixes from hestia.rs:467-488 and work_decisions.rs:287-291. Shapes tests catch a rewording, but every new generator that cites text needs a new hand-written skip in reading.rs. Decision 10's audit is the stand-in for that. Fix: In D164 under Alternatives or Reversal cost, name the general fix: generators mark cited content with a shared delimiter or constant that reading.rs reads. Propose it as follow-up work, since hestia.rs and work_decisions.rs are outside this job's deliverables.

summary: I read the code; I ran nothing. The plan matches the accepted reading and holds up against the code. These all exist where the plan says: refusing_check and its step! lines (reading.rs:3228-3254), request_words (3507), check_outcome_state and its doc tests (3653-3680, 8358-8437), replay_limit_percent (5005), replay_problem (producer.rs:49-68), approve_request with its anchor sentence and fixed lines (work_decisions.rs:279-313), and the hestia root-cause shapes (hestia.rs:458-507). It also correctly found that request_words splits `layer_count` on `_`, so stripping code-like tokens is needed. hestia, work_decisions, store and steward are public modules. athena-git, jiff and tempfile are normal dependencies of athena-core, so the corpus helpers can build the real generators. The demonstrations run the real gate, and each would fail without the behavior. No existing corpus or CLI request uses the four words, apart from 7bf8 and the approval text the plan handles. One reader of the changed gate is missing from the dependents list. steward::queued_work, which serves the drain and `athena plan`, re-runs check_reading_text on the stored readings of proposed requests (steward.rs:415-427). Any queued request whose stored reading predates this check, and whose plain prose uses tier, layer, ladder or rung, will drop out of the queue with no message until a person runs `athena go`. That has to be listed, tested and stated in the docs. One minor gap: criterion 7's measured-share wording is not written into the docs when a send-back happens. The anchor-gated skips of generated text are a reasonable answer to the deliverables limit, and the shapes tests guard them. The tier and layer false refusals are the user's chosen list and are flagged openly.
